sc4_db_outage_and_failover.workers: All three processes stayed alive for the whole outage. Each worker logged one WARN per pass per queue: upload finalize drain, transcode drain, video import drain, account export drain/sweep, process heartbeat write, settings version poll. 34 and 35 lines respectively over ~40 s.
sc4_db_outage_and_failover.backoff_finding: There is NO backoff ladder. internal/jobloop retries at its FIXED interval for as long as the outage lasts — the transcode drain's failures are 10.000 s apart, exactly its tick (12:44:23.23, :33.23, :43.23, :53.23, 12:45:03.23, :13.23). The log rate is therefore constant and proportional to (workers x loops), not decaying. Bounded and harmless at this size; recorded because A34's brief assumed a ladder.

sc6_copy_checksums_resume_abort.surface: POST/GET/POST-cancel on /api/v1/admin/storage/migrations[/{id}][/cancel], admin-only. The operator reads state, source_desc, target_desc, objects_total/done/failed, last_error, observed_cutover_at and a per-state object breakdown. There is NO start/cancel control in vidra-user — AdminInfrastructureView renders the campaign list read-only (getStorageMigrations); starting and cancelling are API-only.
sc6_copy_checksums_resume_abort.verification: Every object is verified END TO END: PutSizedHashed digests the bytes as READ FROM THE SOURCE, then the object is re-opened FROM THE TARGET and re-hashed, and the two must agree; a video_files.sha256 cross-check is a third opinion. Six randomly sampled keys were checked independently — ledger sha256 == local file sha256 == sha256 of the object read back through the S3 API — 6/6.

injected_failure.method: a MinIO user booted with the readwrite policy, then downgraded to readonly WHILE the workers ran, then 54 new objects created by an upload
injected_failure.observed: all 54 objects went pending -> attempts=1, last_error 'copy failed; retrying'; worker WARN 'storage migration could not copy an object; will retry' with error 'storage: s3: put "...": Access Denied. [write_denied]'
injected_failure.recovery: policy restored 13:16:38; the objects retried on their 1-minute backoff at ~13:17:12 and all 54 verified; the campaign reached synced at 13:18:08 with 1272/1272 and objects_failed 0
injected_failure.operator_visibility_gap: while the 54 objects were failing the campaign showed state=copying, objects_done 1218, objects_total 1272, objects_failed 0 and last_error "" — the per-object reason exists (the short fixed categories were designed to be projected) but NO surface projects it. The admin jobs overview shows the object ledger as a queue (storage_migrations pending/running/done/failed) and nothing more.
injected_failure.boot_refusal: SEPARATE and more serious: a migration target the process cannot WRITE to is a FATAL BOOT REFUSAL, not a paused campaign. Booting the api with the read-only credential produced 'fatal error=storage migration target: storage: s3: check bucket "vidra-a34": Access Denied. [write_denied]' and the process exited before the listener opened — /healthz answered nothing at all. Both workers did the same. An operator who rotates or narrows the target bucket's credential cannot start ANY process.

defect_found_and_fixed.what: A SECOND campaign enumerated ZERO objects and announced 'synced' — 'every object in the source is verified in the target' with objects_total 0 — because storage_migration_objects is primary-keyed on the STORAGE KEY alone, the previous campaign's rows outlive it, and the enumeration is an ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING upsert.
defect_found_and_fixed.measured: campaign e33d7808 started at 12:50:39 against a source of 1191 objects, logged 'storage migration enumerated the source store objects=0' at 12:51:01 and 'storage migration is synced ... objects=0' at 12:52:01, with 136 of 1191 objects in the destination
defect_found_and_fixed.blast_radius: it bites a retry after an abort AND the second move an instance ever makes — a bucket-to-bucket migration after a local-to-bucket one re-uses exactly the same keys, so the done campaign's rows swallow the whole enumeration and the operator is told it is safe to cut over
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: vidra-core#224 — Start clears the ledger of every campaign that is OVER before the new one enumerates; the DELETE's predicate is on the CAMPAIGN's state so it can never touch a live ledger; unit + integration regressions, both RED before and GREEN after
defect_found_and_fixed.reverified: campaign 57a35fd3, started against the same 1191-object source plus the aborted campaign's 136 leftovers, enumerated all of them and ran to done with 1272/1272

sc7_reads_switch_retention.reads_during_movement: a 5 Hz loop over three media URLs (poster, CMAF chunk, HLS master) ran for the whole slice: 26,412 samples, 26,211 x 200 and 201 x 000 (connection refused). ZERO 404s and ZERO 5xx. Every 000 falls inside one of five DELIBERATE process restarts.
sc7_reads_switch_retention.dual_read: reads during movement are served by storage.Fallback (cmd/api/main.go): the HTTP media handle — and only it — tries the primary and falls back to the other store on a definite miss. mediagc, the IPFS mirror, the doctor and every media tool keep the RAW primary, and presigned delivery is disabled outright while a migration target is configured ('direct object delivery disabled while a storage migration target is configured').

authority_switch.mechanism: the operator swaps BOTH env sets (STORAGE_* now names the bucket, STORAGE_MIGRATION_TARGET_* names the old local root) and restarts; the campaign READS the swap off its two handles rather than being told
authority_switch.window: 3 failed requests inside ONE second (13:18:58), all code 000 — the process restart. No 404 window at all; the api answered again within the same second, and the three URLs returned identical byte counts (8727 / 35179 / 1636) before and after.
authority_switch.observed: cutover recorded at 13:19:58.921 — 60 s after the restart, because the sweep that notices it is the LEADER-GATED 1-minute ticker. 'storage migration cutover observed: the api is now serving from the migration target serving=s3://... source_deleted_after=1h0m0s'

sc7_reads_switch_retention.retention: with STORAGE_MIGRATION_GRACE_HOURS=1 the old local store kept all 1272 files and 302,584 KB through cutover and beyond; nothing was deleted until the operator's explicit change
sc7_reads_switch_retention.rollback_before_expiry: swapping both env sets BACK at 13:20:47 restored local authority with ZERO read failures and identical byte counts. The campaign noticed and said so on the admin surface: last_error 'the api is serving from this migration's source again, so the cutover was undone; finish the environment swap or cancel this migration', plus ERROR 'storage migration is past cutover but the api is serving from the migration SOURCE again; nothing will be deleted'. Source still 1272 files.
sc7_reads_switch_retention.release: the operator set STORAGE_MIGRATION_GRACE_HOURS=0 and swapped forward again at 13:22:29. deleting_source opened at 13:23:33 and removed 200 objects per leader sweep (13:24:31, :25:31, :26:31, :27:31, :28:31, :29:31, then 72 at 13:30:31), reaching done at 13:30:32 with source_deleted 1272, objects_failed 0, local root 0 files and the bucket at 1273 (1272 + .vidra/owner).

sc8_gc_interlock.during_copy: POST /admin/media/gc {"dry_run": false} at 12:59:09 answered {"dry_run": true, "mode": "dry-run", "scanned": 1191, "deleted": 0, "forced_dry_run": true, "forced_dry_run_reason": "storage_migration_active"} — the interlock NAMES ITSELF in the response body
sc8_gc_interlock.audit: admin.media.gc success reason 'mode=dry-run scanned=1272 orphans=0 orphan_pct=0 deleted=0 breaker=false ownership=owned forced_dry_run=true forced_reason=storage_migration_active' — so it is not silent in the audit trail either
sc8_gc_interlock.ui: AdminMediaView renders the reason verbatim: 'A storage migration campaign is in flight, so the two stores are deliberately out of step and an object with no database reference is not evidence about either of them (an unanswerable migration check counts as one running). Wait for the campaign to finish, or cancel it, then purge again.'
sc8_gc_interlock.masking_note: during CUTOVER the same request reported forced_reason=bucket_ownership instead, because the ownership gate is evaluated FIRST and the destination bucket carried no marker yet (the migration writes it at completion). Same outcome (deleted 0) but a reason that points an operator at adoption. After adopting the bucket explicitly the very next destructive sweep reported forced_reason=storage_migration_active with ownership=owned — so both rails are live and the FIRST one to fire is the one named.
sc8_gc_interlock.after_release: with the campaign done the same request ran for real: mode 'delete', scanned 1272, orphans 0, deleted 0, forced_dry_run false
sc8_gc_interlock.collects_exactly_the_released: one video was then deleted through the API (204). The dry run listed exactly 27 orphans, ALL of them that video's keys; the destructive sweep deleted exactly those 27 (bucket 1300 -> 1273) and the other videos' media still answered 200 with unchanged byte counts.
sc8_gc_interlock.orphan_breaker: unaffected — orphan_percent 2 against MEDIA_GC_MAX_ORPHAN_PERCENT 90, breaker_tripped false throughout

findings: A migration target the process cannot WRITE to is a FATAL BOOT REFUSAL for the api AND the workers, so a rotated or narrowed target credential takes the whole instance down with no HTTP at all.
An anonymous read during a PostgreSQL outage answers a bare 500 internal_error; the authenticated path is typed 503 session_store_unavailable (A17/core#180). The anonymous half was never typed.
internal/jobloop has no backoff ladder: every loop retries at its fixed interval for as long as a dependency is down, so the WARN rate is constant and scales with workers x loops.

A campaign whose objects are failing shows objects_failed 0 and last_error "" until the attempt budget is spent; the short fixed failure categories were designed to be projected into an operator surface and no surface projects them.

storage_migration_objects rows survive their campaign and nothing deletes them even after the fix (the fix clears them at the START of the next campaign), so the per-state breakdown of a terminal campaign zeroes out once a later campaign begins; the campaign row's own counters remain the record.

The storage-migration worker WARN redacts object_key into '[redacted-key]' and then prints the same key verbatim inside the error string ('storage: s3: put "thumbnails/<uuid>.jpg": Access Denied') — a concrete instance of A35's open 'core still logs object_key/storage_key in the storage-migration paths'.

storage_migrations IS projected into job_runs (a trigger on the table), contradicting A17's list; but the projected rows carry EMPTY correlation_id, request_id and worker_id, so the campaign cannot be tied back to the admin request that started it.
vidra-user has no control that starts or cancels a storage migration — AdminInfrastructureView lists campaigns read-only. Both write actions are API-only.
An aborted campaign leaves its partial copies on the destination forever; nothing in the product removes them.
not_run: A real provider bucket (B2/S3) — no credentials on this machine; MinIO stands in, so provider versioning, object lock and lifecycle remain untested, as STO-01 already records
A genuinely SEPARATE host for the second worker — both workers are processes on one machine, so a real network partition between worker and store was not exercised
vidra-user's admin surfaces in a browser: the storage-migration UI is a read-only list and every action this slice needed is API-only, so no Chromium run was warranted
A bucket-to-bucket (s3 -> s3) campaign; the local -> s3 direction is what the row names
